judgment.rationale: The original author reports the Image Resizer context-menu action is inert on 0.75.1 across two Windows 10 PCs while 0.72.1 and 0.74.x worked; later commenters confirm failures on 0.77.0 and 0.80.1, including a progress bar that closes immediately. This is enough for a current-build maintainer reproduction.
evidence: The original body says selecting Image Resize from the JPG context menu does nothing on two Windows 10 22H2 PCs, and downgrading to 0.72.1 restored it.
The author attached Windows Error Reporting, .NET Runtime, and Application event files; their contents were not inspected.
A commenter reports the same issue on PowerToys 0.77.0.
A second commenter reports that on 0.80.1 the progress bar flashes and closes.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the context-menu launch and capture the resizer process lifetime on a current build before investigating the startup failure path.

fix_assessment.rationale: The repeated version-specific behavior supports investigating launch/startup regressions, but the issue body and event-file references do not establish the failing component or exact root cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore reliable Image Resizer context-menu startup
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the Image Resizer context-menu invocation may be launching a process that exits during startup on affected builds. The progress bar flash reported on 0.80.1 is consistent with, but does not prove, a startup exception or initialization failure.
plan: On a current supported build, invoke Image Resize from Explorer for one JPG and then multiple JPGs; observe whether the UI process starts and exits.
Repeat on the reporter's Windows 10 configuration if available, and compare with a known-working version only if the test environment can safely provide it.
Trace the context-menu activation through the Image Resizer startup and error handling path; use the already-attached event data only if needed for diagnosis.
If a startup failure is confirmed, fix the failing initialization path and add regression coverage for single- and multi-image launches.
verification: The Image Resizer interface remains open after selecting one or more JPG files from Explorer.
The operation completes without a briefly flashing progress window or silent exit.
Verify the context-menu launch on Windows 10 and Windows 11 where supported.

confidence.rationale: Multiple reporters and versions show a consistent failure, but no current-build reproduction or inspected event evidence establishes why the process exits.

issue_context.summary: The Image Resizer context-menu command reportedly does nothing or briefly displays progress then closes, while older releases worked for the original reporter.
known_information: The original report is PowerToys 0.75.1 on Windows 10 22H2, reproduced on two PCs; JPG selection is specified.
The author reports 0.72.1 worked and 0.74.x also worked, while 0.75.1 did not.
Later comments confirm the symptom on 0.77.0 and 0.80.1.
The original report includes three Windows event attachments; their contents have not been opened or analyzed.
inferences: The repeated progress-window exit suggests a launch/startup failure, but does not identify whether the UI, shell integration, or image processing path is responsible.
A regression window may lie after the 0.74.x series, but the issue does not identify the first failing release.
issue_context.analysis: The issue has enough evidence to reproduce without asking for another log package. Use the attached event references only if a current test narrows the startup failure.
initial_investigation: Read the full body and both comments and noted the three linked Windows event files without opening their contents.
Reviewed the current Image Resizer context-menu ownership area; no evidence in the issue establishes a code-level root cause.

reproduce.version_requirement: Use a current supported PowerToys build; historical reports include 0.75.1, 0.77.0, and 0.80.1.
prerequisites: A JPG test image and a second JPG for multi-selection.
steps: Select one JPG in Explorer, invoke Image Resize, and observe whether the resizer interface stays open.
If the process exits, note whether the progress UI flashes and compare the application behavior when invoked from the module settings.
reproduce.expected: The Image Resizer interface opens and remains available to complete the resize operation.

actions.label: Approve launch-path investigation
actions.note: Repeated historical reports justify reproduction; startup root cause remains red.
